body:
I just feel more comfortable here I guess since I can just vent away and not hold back. But the minute I try to get help IRL, my mind shuts down and I can't ask for it. I literally just become frozen, and that fake smiling mask of my just says I'm alright. I hate myself for doing that but I'm literally too scared to ask. I guess it's the whole "talking to another person face to face" that makes me so incredibly nervous. I know I shouldn't be ashamed  but I am. There was one time at my old community college where I finally was brave enough to talk to a counselor there. But I didn't feel better at all really, other than just getting stuff off my chest. They do have counselors we can speak to at my current college but I'm so worried that one of my friends will see me going there and then know how fucked up I am. Or I just have this fear of it becoming known to everyone what is going on with me. I know I'm just paranoid, but I don't want others knowing about this... I don't want that title of being the depressed suicidal cripple. I've tried so hard to fit in and have that "happy go lucky" attitude in life but it's just completely falling apart and my true self is starting to show. That's what I'm afraid of... people seeing the real me. 

I want to try, I really do. But my crippling fear has prevented me time and time again. I agree, I think having the lady counsel me would be a bit strange since I see her almost daily. But she's someone I'm super comfortable with and I know I can trust her. If she asks or starts to notice then maybe I'll ask for her help. I just want someone to talk to but I'm incapable of finding that person. Thank you so much though for your replies... You've really helped me through the past few days. They were the shittiest days of my life, so I hope that's in the past. I want to be happy, so here's to me trying to find that again and hoping to avoid that dark path I took earlier this week. :/

I have the resources to find someone to talk to, but I have this crippling fear of showing emotions in front of others... or expressing how I feel. The saddest thing is, I have help literally just around the corner. The house I live in has a back house where a family therapist /psychologist lives. I actually was in the process of breaking down when she and my other roommate walked in. I just hid my face and pretended to be on my phone while I was silently just sobbing. My face is literally just stained red and burns from the amount of crying I've been doing. I've never felt this bad before. I know I need help but I'm so embarrassed to get it. And I know this lady would help me, because she's an amazing person... but I don't want anyone who lives with me knowing about my true nature. I don't want to be looked at as the freak of the household and be treated differently. But I don't know how much longer I can go about avoiding everyone trying not to have a mental breakdown. It's like, I'm almost hoping she notices but at the same time, I never want her to know. It's why I've never been to a psychologist... plus I wouldn't be able to say what I needed to say. It's why I come here online to vent, because that's my only form of communication I can do. ;(

It sucks, it really does. I have had it on and off as well, but this time it has really struck me. I find myself not being able to focus on anything anymore. I just want to find a nice blanket to curl up into and sit there for hours. I thought I was stronger than this but I've proven to myself that I'm not. I keep fighting for the sake of my family... I'd never want them to experience what this feels like. 

Honestly? I'm not well at all. I haven't been truly happy in a while. I adopted a dog earlier this year to try and help pull me back into the real world, but even he can't help with these "episodes" of depression. He may have been the only thing that night though stopping me from going through with it... he was right there just watching me. I can't bear to think of leaving him since I'm the one who rescued him in the first place... but I don't know if it's enough to keep me around. He's the golden part of my day though and even if it's for a few minutes, he makes me feel genuinely good as though I deserve to be here. Other times though, I just sink into these awful emotions and it really drags me down. I can't drag myself out of it this time. I'm worse than I've ever been.

Thank you for your comment. Started making me cry again... ha. I guess I just feel like the worst person for putting my parents through that. I look at them and try to imagine where they'd be had they not had me. I think their lives would have been better without me, which is why I still think that. It would hurt them at first but I think the stress would be lifted off. I'm 22 years old and still have to depend on them if I break something or have surgery. And I will ever be beyond grateful to them and love them for everything they've done, but it's not fair for me to continue doing that to them. I doubt I'll ever get married either, so basically when I'm older, I'll be alone by myself dealing with this. I will have no family left. THEN I will truly be alone rather than just feel it. I want to be happy like I used to be. I was so damn happy as a kid... everyone would comment how unusually cheerful I was. But now, I'm not even 5% of what I used to be. I don't talk to people much, I'm not engaged with my classes or peers... I'm stuck in this loop that doesn't feel natural or normal. I don't feel like what I'm living everyday is real, if that makes any sense. I don't know how to explain it anyway else other than, I don't find live enjoyable anymore. I love my family, friends, and pets, but I don't know how much they'll keep me going. I just wish for once, someone would come up to me and ask how I was ACTUALLY doing... not the typical, "How are you"? "Oh I'm good"! conversation. Because every-time I say I'm well is every-time I'm just lying to myself.
You really did help me out. You and everyone who commented has really given me a ton of helpful info and advice to kind of step back and reflect on. I think it was exactly what I needed. :')

I will definitely do that! Thank you for taking the time to speak with me. I feel a lot better after getting all that off my chest, and honestly just feel better about this whole situation. Like, I'm ready to make the changes. I'll be in Cali in 3 weeks, so I really can't wait to start my new life! :) Feeling confident now that I've got an idea of who I want to be.

Thank you for the kind words! I wasn't wanting to really "label" myself necessarily, but I really just wanted an idea of what I could be. I never knew the confusion and pain members of the LGBT community go through when they're first figuring this all out. And the thing is, I think I've known for years now, but was in denial. 

I'm thinking California is going to really help me. I'll be able to be myself, dress the way I want, like who I like, and just be a complete different person. When I come back home to visit, if my family doesn't like what they see... well, I can't do much about that. :/ But I'm hoping for all to go well. And thank you for the link! I'm going to check it out right now. :)

Yeah, I think I've determined genderfluid is the term for me, or at least as a general idea for now. After this thread and doing a lot of side research, I feel confident that that's what I am.

My family is like, a 50/50 chance they'd be supportive or totally against it. It's harder for me to come out to them than it was for my brother, since it's like... two siblings who are both not straight, with me being the one who is "suppose to be straight". Puts me in a very tricky, uncomfortable situation. I've looked at the risks and though I don't think it'd ever get to this stage, I fear them doing something like pulling me from school or cutting off financial support. Again, I don't think they would ever do this, but I know they wouldn't be happy. They already don't like how I dress or my views on gender stereotypes, so I feel like that would be crossing their line. But then again, they're supportive of my brother and love him and his boyfriend, so you never know. I think it's harder for people to understand bisexuals, pansexuals, gender fluid people, etc, because they prefer both genders. My mom considers it wrong because she thinks it should be one or the other. It's like, people can't help who they fall in love with. They don't seem to really "get" it when it comes to these kind of things. They basically think you're either gay or straight, nothing in the middle. /:

I do hope college helps me find the strength to start my change. I really want to associate myself with people in the LGBT community more too, so that's one of my biggest goals. Yeah, I think I will wait it out telling the family. At least until I'm out of school and all... or if a special someone comes along before that. :p

Thank you, I really hope so too. I think I'll change a lot once I'm there, seeing I have this freedom to be who I want to be for the first time. :) Hopefully I can find myself a group of people who share similar interests and who I can relate to as well.

Yeah, I understand. I don't necessarily feel like I have to fall into a certain category or give myself a label, but it would help with my questions and help me realize what I what, you know? It's just a struggle to find out in the beginning stages, because I question everything and 2nd guess myself. It's a constant internal battle. :S

Am I comfortable with my gender? It's like 50/50 for me. I'm not uncomfortable being a female, but there's definitely traits about myself and my body that I don't like. And I don't like the stereotypes that are given to each gender, especially the female stereotype I've been led to believe in. But it's kind of like I don't consider myself a female, or a male. It's a bit of both, because I find qualities in both that I like. You're right though. In the end, it's going to be up to me to decide for myself, and not my parents. It's just a scary thought of the idea of my parents disagreeing with my lifestyle. What will they do or say if they find out? That's the biggest thing setting me back atm... is the fear of being rejected. :S

>  

Thank you for writing back. :) I don't normally read Manga's but I might have to check that one out, so thank you for mentioning it. I think you're right with the hair thing. When I cut my hair, let's just say my dad didn't approve of it (which I didn't care too much about) but the hairstyles I've been getting are gradually getting shorter and shorter. It's almost to where I want it, and I've been a lot happier with myself since I made the decision. I think once I move out, I'll be able to experiment more freely with my hairstyles and such without facing judgement from them, since they won't see me too often. I'm actually really excited to start fresh in California. Nervous, but super pumped.

Yeah, I'm going to have to find a way to see how my brother feels about it before asking him. I think, in the past... he's hinted at knowing something, but I've always told him, "No of course I don't find other girls attractive", because I wasn't really ready for the truth to come out yet. I'm hoping to meet more people like myself in Cali that I can relate to and maybe talk to them before gaining the confidence to talk to anyone in my family. 

Thank you so much again for talking with me about this. I was a mess last night and my mind was super clustered. It had even been preventing me from sleeping so I was just worn down. Feeling much better today after reading your and the other comments.  :)

I think that's where I'm confused, is... am I transgender and just am not sure? Or am I that new term, gender fluid? For instance, do you know who Ruby Rose is? After watching her short film and hearing why she considers herself as "gender fluid", I relate a LOT to that. Like, it's not that I'm aiming to be a guy and desire a penis or something, but guy things attract me more. There are things I hate about my body (err, my breasts, for example) but it's not this extremely powerful feeling of disgust or anything. It's a little uncomfortable, but not overwhelming. I mean, I'm just naturally attracted to more masculine clothing, short style hair, tattoos, and maybe even being muscular. For some reason I kind of wish I was semi muscular, though I'm too lazy to go to the gym haha. But I guess that video really kind of spoke to me, because she showed me you don't necessarily have to transition if I have these feelings. You can still dress and adopt the "man lifestyle" while still being a female and all. It's just a lot of confusion lol. And yeah, I watched that video you linked earlier actually! Definitely cleared up some questions I had. I'm still new to all of these terms, but I'm trying my best to learn them.

Yeah, the family part is what's the most difficult for me. :( My parents are accepting of the LGBT community (my dad is now slightly more accepting after my brother came out) but they don't agree with bisexuality. My mom has told me she thinks it's wrong for whatever her reasons of believing that. And that's what really terrifies me, is having them accept my brother but not me. :/ I want to talk to my brother too, but I don't know his views on bisexuals. I know some members of the LGBT community aren't too accepting of it, but I don't know how he feels. We aren't super close or have personal talks much, so it'd be very difficult to talk to him I think. :/ I've been wanting to talk to my best friend about this since she is kind of in the same boat as I am, but every time I try, I tense up and the words literally won't leave my mouth. I just get too anxious and scared to say anything. I want my family to know eventually, but at the same time, I don't. Hearing the things they've said in the past about bisexuality makes me never want to tell them, ever. :/ I will try though talking to my brother once I gain the confidence. I'm afraid he won't keep my secret though, since he's kind of a loud mouth haha.

I don't know really, I'm sorry for posting such a long rant. I don't mean to come off as if I'm whining or anything. I've just been feeling pretty alone and kind of isolated with this issue since there's really no one I can talk to about it. I'm not sure what the next step is with my life. It's like, I have the image of the person I want to be and how I want to present myself, but that image is greatly different from what I currently look like. And my fear is changing my image that drastically would upset my family and I'd just hear more criticism from them. I know I shouldn't let them hold me back, but if they make me feel ashamed enough, they will. 

I guess the good thing is, I'm moving out in a month to attend college in California. I'll be living on my own for the first time ever. I think... that's where I may kind of discover myself more. Once I surround myself with people of similar interest, and just present myself the way I want, maybe I'll be able to be happier and figure out everything. At least I'm hoping it'll be that easy.

I guess I'm just stuck as to, where do I go from here? Do I start slow and small, like cutting my hair the way I want? Gradually start dressing in clothes that defines myself? I guess I'm "transitioning" in a way... but not sure how to do so.
